lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Several bullets wrap awkwardly, including a split hyphenated word.
items.because: Awkward wrapping can look poor and interfere with ATS parsing.

items.says: Use consistent punctuation, capitalization, tense, and date formatting throughout.
Keep the résumé to one page unless there is substantial additional experience.
items.because: That length suits this career stage.

items.says: Prioritize credible business outcomes over Lighthouse scores and implementation details.
Ensure the code URL leads to a live, polished portfolio or GitHub profile.
items.because: It should not be a generic or incomplete link.

items.says: Consider adding LinkedIn if the profile is complete.
items.because: It could support the candidacy.

items.says: Confirm that the email, phone number, and URL are clickable in the PDF.
Use a date style consistent with the rest of the document.
Check that the experience and project dates fit the actual submission date.
items.because: The M.S. is listed as in progress.

items.says: Consider adding the M.S. GPA if it is strong and helpful.
Consider visually consolidating the school name across the two degrees.
items.because: Both degrees are from the same institution, so this could save space and reduce repetition.

items.says: If space is limited, show only the B.S. graduation date.
items.because: Employers usually care more about completion than the start date.

items.says: Add B.S. honors if they are meaningful.
Confirm the internship dates and whether the role is completed.
items.because: If it is ongoing, the end date and bullet tenses should reflect that.

items.says: Use the employer’s exact title if “Frontend Engineering Intern” was not official.
items.because: A different title could cause discrepancies during verification.

items.says: Clarify what “load time” measures.
items.because: It could mean server response, page load, or a user-centric metric.

items.says: Specify whether the 9% bookings-per-search increase is relative or in percentage points.
Include the A/B test’s duration, sample size, or statistical confidence if available.
items.because: That would make the causal claim more credible.

items.says: Say whether the JavaScript figures are compressed transfer sizes or uncompressed bundle sizes.
items.because: The metrics are otherwise difficult to interpret.

items.says: Add a measured user or business impact if available.
Verify that both widgets were excluded from the initial bundle.
items.because: They might merely have been split into separate files.

items.says: Identify the accessibility standard or audit basis if known.
Make the scope of “all 14” clear.
items.because: One audit does not establish universal accessibility.

items.says: Add the resulting audit outcome or user impact if available.
Rewrite the awkward opening construction as a direct action-result statement.
items.because: That would match the other bullets.

items.says: Shorten or split the list of four optimizations.
items.because: The implementation details obscure the main accomplishment.

items.says: State whether the Lighthouse scores used the same device, network, and test conditions.
Present the Lighthouse score as a lab result unless there is field data.
items.because: It is not a definitive production-user result.

items.says: Lazy-loading the hero image does not support the claimed LCP improvement.
items.because: It usually delays loading an above-the-fold LCP image.

items.says: Say whether the LCP result came from production field data or a controlled lab test.
Add the scale of the token documentation.
items.because: The number of tokens, components, designers, or teams affected is unclear.

items.says: Add a measurable impact if possible.
items.because: The result is weaker than the quantified performance bullets.

items.says: Verify that “Web Developer” was the official title.
Check that the claimed scope is plausible for the roughly five-month role.
Converting PNG images to WebP cannot reduce a JavaScript bundle by 60%.
items.because: It can reduce image payload or total page weight, not JavaScript bundle size.

items.says: Clarify how many university sites were affected.
Clarify the attribution from interviews to preview mode to fewer broken-page reports.
items.because: The wording implies a direct causal chain.

items.says: State the comparison period for the drop from 30 to 6 reports a month.
items.because: Otherwise it could be read as a one-month fluctuation.

items.says: “Writes” is in the wrong tense for this ended role.
items.because: The verb should be past tense.

items.says: Clarify whether you created, maintained, or applied the checklist.
items.because: “Writes” is vague.

items.says: Define what the 12-to-2 failed-audit figure counts.
items.because: It could refer to pages, issues, sites, or audit cycles.

items.says: Support the causal link between the checklist and fewer failed audits.
items.because: Other changes may also have contributed.

items.says: Define “search time.”
items.because: It could mean response latency, time to display results, or time to find a course.

items.says: Explain how client-side filtering handled catalog size and data freshness if relevant.
State the number of courses or records.
items.because: That would show scale.

items.says: Make the technology labels consistent with the Skills section and the technologies used.
Add a live link and repository link if the project is public.
Define how the roughly 900 weekly riders are counted.
items.because: They might be unique users, sessions, or devices.

items.says: Verify that “live” arrivals are real-time rather than scheduled estimates.
Consider naming the data source or transit API.
items.because: It could demonstrate integration work.

items.says: Calling the drop from 3.0s to 1.5s a 75% improvement is incorrect.
items.because: It is a 50% reduction.

items.says: Offline caching does not explain a true first-time cold-start improvement.
items.because: A first-time load cannot use an existing cache.

items.says: Identify exactly what was measured and under what test conditions.
Verify that stop-list caching was the primary cause of the improvement.
Calling a rise from 30% to 40% a 10% increase is incorrect.
items.because: It is 10 percentage points, or approximately 33% relative.

items.says: Define “returning riders” and the comparison cohorts.
Be cautious about attributing the whole increase to saved stops.
items.because: That attribution needs an experiment or other evidence.

items.says: Include more data if available.
items.because: A one-month observation period is short.

items.says: The project heading says Vue, but the first bullet says React and TypeScript.
items.because: The listed stack contradicts itself.

items.says: Verify the February-to-March hackathon dates.
items.because: That duration may invite questions unless it was a multiweek event.

items.says: React and TypeScript conflict with the Vue project heading.
Replace “Worked on” with the specific scope you owned without duplicating the next bullet.
items.because: The phrase is vague and understates the contribution.

items.says: Add an outcome or scale if available.
Specify the type or extent of testing and its result.
items.because: Coverage of edge cases or defects prevented would make the claim clearer.

items.says: Explain “handling” in measurable or technical terms.
Prevent “time-zone” from splitting across lines in the PDF.
Add the result of the presentation or handoff, or remove the bullet if space is needed and there was no meaningful result.
items.because: The bullet currently lacks impact.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It is not the proper product name.

items.says: Change the “Tools” category label.
items.because: The list mixes a programming language, frameworks, and a development tool.

items.says: Keep Angular only if you can discuss meaningful experience with it.
items.because: Nothing else on the résumé demonstrates it.

items.says: Keep Vue only if the Library Room Booking project actually used it.
items.because: That project’s stack is contradictory.

items.says: Add other relevant frontend, testing, version-control, build, or API skills only if you can use them confidently.
Order the skills by relevance and proficiency.
items.because: The current order appears arbitrary.

items.says: Use a more accurate category label than “Methods.”
items.because: The items mix rendering architecture, a quality discipline, and a testing practice.

items.says: Be more specific about accessibility knowledge if applicable.
items.because: Standards, audits, semantic HTML, or assistive-technology testing would clarify the skill.

items.says: Name the component-testing tools if they are genuine strengths.
Consider demonstrating these items in bullets rather than a separate skills category.
